clue.text: John and I can give up the job

parts.note: Jack is a familiar form of the name John
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Someone called John and the speaker are able to resign their posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' reads as a verb but is the noun, a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack something in is an informal idiom for quitting, here quitting work.

clue.text: In Paris I petition a Catholic…

parts.note: the French word for I is je
a suit is a formal petition or plea

explanation.surface: A French speaker begins to appeal to a Catholic, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Society of Jesus is a Roman Catholic priest of that order.

clue.text: … minister to arrange a truce

indicators.note: to arrange the letters of the words is to set them in a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a Catholic asks a clergyman to broker a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue's surface to 1-down but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant parish priest is a minister of the Church.

clue.text: Angry Hibernian militants take note

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army; Hibernian means Irish
te is a note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt ti

explanation.surface: Furious Irish paramilitaries make a written note.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: furious, cross.

clue.text: Briefly, where an electrical fault may lie

definitions.meaning: a phrase meaning to put it concisely

definitions.text: where an electrical fault may lie
definitions.meaning: a short circuit is a common wiring fault, so the trouble lies in a short

explanation.surface: Put concisely, here is where the wiring problem is.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to sum up concisely, and literally places a fault inside a short circuit.

clue.text: Irishman's without a house. Pity!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the Irishman's name goes round the house

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish name; with the possessive it gives PATS

explanation.surface: An Irishman is homeless, and what a shame that is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside': PATS surrounds HO.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality that arouses sorrow or compassion in an audience.

clue.text: Inclined to describe the ratio of sin to cos?

definitions.meaning: sloping, not upright

definitions.text: the ratio of sin to cos
definitions.meaning: sine divided by cosine is the tangent, or tan, of an angle

explanation.surface: A trigonometry student wonders how to describe sine over cosine.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as A TAN ANGLE: an angle's tan is its sine over its cosine.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means tilted or slanting, and punningly names a tangent of an angle.

clue.text: Man married women from the Western Isles

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
brides are women newly married

explanation.surface: A man weds several women who come from Scotland's islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are the islands off Scotland's west coast, officially the Western Isles.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name of the island chain off north-west Scotland.

clue.text: Leave present

definitions.meaning: to depart on a journey
to state or lay out, as an argument

explanation.surface: Two terse commands: go away, and put something forward.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to begin a journey and to expound an idea.

clue.text: A wild grass in so calm a sea of vegetation

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the word so, which wraps it
wild letters run free and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Untamed grass grows in a sea so still that it is all plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' shuffles the clue's opening A and its grass, and 'in' sets that mix inside so. The Sargasso Sea in the Atlantic is famously calm and covered in floating seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: This Atlantic region is known for still waters and mats of floating seaweed.

clue.text: Cunning move resulting from overriding ambition

indicators.note: the letters come straight out of the words that follow, lying inside them

explanation.surface: A crafty manoeuvre is the product of overwhelming ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess opening or any calculated ploy that gives something up for advantage.

clue.text: Frisk a college servant

definitions.meaning: to gambol or caper about
at Trinity College Dublin a ... is a student's servant

explanation.surface: Search a member of the college staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisk' suggests a body search but means to caper. A skip is a college servant at Trinity College Dublin, like a scout at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to hop lightly, and the noun names a Dublin college attendant.

clue.text: Where wharf-labourers are employed on trial

definitions.meaning: dockers work at the docks
an accused person stands ... in a criminal court

explanation.surface: A place for dockworkers, and also someone facing the court.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase places workers at a quayside and a defendant in the courtroom enclosure.

clue.text: In the morning I take no protein ingredient

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon
taken as written

explanation.surface: At breakfast time the speaker declines something.
explanation.definitionFit: Amino acids are the building blocks from which proteins are made.

clue.text: Discharge when prison term is over

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for a sentence is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: doing time means serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: Release comes when a sentence has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' seems to mean finished but is the instruction to turn TIME round.
explanation.definitionFit: To send out or give off, as a device does light or gas.

clue.text: Produced an after-dinner sweet and coined in the cash

definitions.meaning: literally manufactured a peppermint
to earn a great deal of money

explanation.surface: A confectioner cooked up a treat and earned a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally confected a peppermint; idiomatically earned a fortune, the Royal Mint being where coins are struck.

clue.text: Colouring suits swineherds tea T

parts.note: men who tend pigs, pigmen

explanation.surface: Dyes that look good on pig keepers, down to a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance giving colour, such as a paint ingredient or natural tint.

clue.text: Biscuits and bananas

definitions.meaning: thin dry savoury biscuits eaten with cheese
slang for crazy, mad

explanation.surface: A snack of crispbread with fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names thin savoury biscuits and is slang for mad.

clue.text: The purpose of a social gathering

definitions.meaning: the role something is designed for
a formal party or reception

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a party is for.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a role or use, and also a formal reception or event.

clue.text: Gather one must take the next whole number

definitions.meaning: to collect together, as cattle or suspects
to round a figure up to the integer above

explanation.surface: Someone must collect things and push a figure up to an integer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to collect together, and in arithmetic to raise to the next integer.

clue.text: Invalid food given to a childish old man

parts.note: pap is soft mushy food for babies or invalids

explanation.surface: Mush is fed to a doddering, second-childhood pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old man' is slang for father, and the answer is the childish word for him; 'Invalid' is the noun, a sick person.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's word for father, the old man being slang for one's dad.

clue.text: Charge an apprentice, but have compassion

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
L is the learner plate sign, a learner being an apprentice

explanation.surface: Bill a trainee, but show some sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be emotionally touched or sympathetic.

clue.text: Dissension caused by dramatised documentary

definitions.meaning: a split into groups within a party
a blend of fact and fiction, as a docudrama

explanation.surface: Disagreement stirred up by a docudrama.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means internal party conflict, and as a blend of fact and fiction names docudrama.

clue.text: A religionist devout in days gone by

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other, the pious one placed within the times past

parts.note: the past is days gone by
pi is informal for pious or devout

explanation.surface: A believer who was pious in former times.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostile old term for a Roman Catholic, follower of the Pope.

clue.text: Thin peel covering Big Apple

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, covering it

parts.note: the skin of a fruit is its peel
nickname for New York, abbreviated NY

explanation.surface: Thin skin wrapped around a large apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym for very slim or lean.

clue.text: Two senior officers taking a drink

parts.note: CO is commanding officer
a second commanding officer, CO

explanation.surface: A pair of high-ranking officers are having a drink together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot chocolate beverage made from cacao powder.

clue.text: Choose a footballer riding shoulder-high

parts.note: to pick is to choose
a back is a defensive football player

explanation.surface: Select a player who is being carried aloft by fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Variant of piggyback: carried on someone's back and shoulders.

clue.text: Farewell to France

parts.note: read as the goodbye a French speaker says, or literally a parting from the country

explanation.surface: A departing traveller bids goodbye to France.
explanation.definitionFit: The French goodbye, literally commending someone to God, used in English too.

clue.text: Egyptian permitted to draw forth

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Egyptian
licit means lawful, allowed

explanation.surface: An Egyptian is allowed to bring something out.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke or draw out a response or information.

clue.text: Twice sight an army formation

parts.note: di- is the Greek-derived prefix meaning two or twice
vision is the faculty of sight

explanation.surface: Seeing double in a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A large military unit of several brigades.

clue.text: A tense resolution from legislative council

indicators.note: resolution in the sense of breaking up and settling into new form

explanation.surface: A nervous motion passed by a parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' looks like a motion passed by the council but signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper house of a parliament, as in the US or ancient Rome.

clue.text: Application shown by manufacturers collectively

definitions.meaning: diligence, hard work
the sector of manufacturing businesses

explanation.surface: Diligence displayed by the manufacturing sector.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means diligent effort and also the manufacturing sector as a whole.
